content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new to the [product_name] Web Editor, although I do have some experience with [product_name] programming. I've made a program for the [product_name] with several hour counters, specifically B071, B089, B091, B092, and B093. I'd like to show the output time of each counter on the home page of the integrated web server on my [product_name]. I'm struggling to figure out how to display these blocks and their output time. Additionally, I don’t really understand what the block types V, VB, VD, and VW mean, nor the significance of the block numbers or formats. Apologies if this seems basic—I’ve searched the [product_name] section of the forum and online. Thanks in advance, PS. I’ve worked as an electrical engineer for over 25 years, so I appreciate your patience.

Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum! For your hour counters, the value is a 32‑bit number, so you should use the VD data type. You'll need to transfer the reading into VM memory using parameter VM mapping.
You can set up the VM memory by going to: Tools > Parameter - VM Mapping
In the [product_name] Web Editor, use the "Scaling Time" element.

That’s really helpful information. I also found the help section on VM Mapping within the [product_name] software. (Realized I should’ve checked there, but wasn’t sure what to look for!) I’ll go through your suggested downloads and review the VM Mapping help docs. Hopefully, I can take it all in! Thank you so far, I’ll update you with my progress.
Quick question: Is the block number referring to the ID or to the address in VM Mapping?
The block number is the address of the operand—in this situation, it’s the address in the VM. If you had a block type Q, the block number might be 1, for example.
Thanks, I’ll spend this evening learning all about VM Mapping. I’ll let you know how it goes.

I got it working—thanks to [user_name]! With your help, I opened Parameter VM Mapping in the [product_name] software under Tools. See the attachment: I entered the required blocks and parameters, then clicked the Help button. That opened the VM Mapping description, which explained how to set everything up. That help view clarified what [user_name] explained. Now, when you add analogue items in the Web Editor, it’s easier to assign the correct data type (VB, VW, or VD) and address, as shown in Parameter VM Mapping. I've created my first web page for the web server and it's working perfectly.
See the attachment to view the web page I designed. Excited for my next projects!
Hello [user_name], Everything looks and sounds great!
This was eye-opening! Thanks for your help!

analysis.insight_summary: The user initially had trouble understanding data types, block numbers, and memory mapping when working with the [product_name] Web Editor to display hour counter outputs on the integrated web server. Through forum discussion, users clarified the difference between block type and address, and emphasized the significance of parameter VM Mapping for memory allocation. In-depth in-software help and support from the community enabled the user to resolve their issues, creating a positive learning outcome.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for an intuitive and well-explained process for mapping internal counters to the web interface, with clear explanations of technical terms and addressing methods, so they can easily build custom web pages that show real-time data.
feature_keywords: block data types (V, VB, VW, VD)
